title: Observation of multiphoton entanglement in resonance fluoresce
authors: Xiao-Long Zhou, Jian Wang, Ze-Min Shen, Dong-Yu Huang, Si-Jian He, Qi-Yang Huang, Yi-Jia Liu, Yu-Shu Chen, Quan Jiang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo
abstract: Resonance fluorescence, the process in which a single two-level quantum emitter interacts with a near-resonant coherent light, is a cornerstone of quantum optics as a paradigmatic light-matter interaction. Quantum phenomena in resonance fluorescence have been accounted for in terms of one- and two-photon processes; however, the physical processes arising from the interaction of a single two-level atom with higher photon numbers remain unexplored experimentally. Here we experimentally reveal the multiphoton scattering nature of resonance fluorescence, which intrinsically gives rise to multiphoton entanglement. By accessing quantum fluctuations in the field emitted from a cavity-quantum electrodynamics system, we resolve third- and fourth-order photon scattering events from a single two-level atom. In the three-photon component, the scattered photons are shown to be genuinely energy-time entangled, as verified by a violation of Svetlichny's inequality. As a demonstration of an application, a quantum secret sharing protocol (QSS) is implemented using this entangled photon source. Our study refines the descriptive framework of resonance fluorescence and broadens the scope of its investigation. It also establishes a fundamentally simple route for generating multiphoton entangled states for quantum information processing and quantum metrology.
summary: This paper experimentally reveals that resonance fluorescence from a single atom exhibits a multiphoton scattering nature, intrinsically generating multiphoton entanglement. By isolating quantum field fluctuations in a cavity QED setup, the authors confirmed genuine tripartite entanglement by violating Svetlichny's inequality. This establishes a simple platform for generating entangled states useful for quantum information processing.
main_problem: To experimentally investigate the multiphoton scattering nature of resonance fluorescence, which is expected to generate intrinsic multiphoton entanglement, as higher-order processes have remained unexplored.
main_result: The authors experimentally demonstrated the multiphoton scattering nature, confirming genuine tripartite entanglement via the violation of Svetlichny's inequality, and showed this source can implement a quantum secret sharing protocol.
method: The experiment uses a single two-level emitter coupled to a cavity, employing a notch filter to isolate quantum fluctuations and measuring higher-order correlations using a Franson-type interferometer.
model_or_system: The system is a single two-level quantum emitter (e.g., $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atom) interacting with near-resonant coherent light within a Fabry–Pérot cavity. The analysis focuses on the quantum fluctuation field ($\hat{\epsilon}$) resulting from the scattering process.
key_observables: Three-photon bunching ($g^{(3)}(0)$), violation of Svetlichny’s inequality ($	ext{SSve} > 4$), and correlation measurements as a function of the mean-field suppression ratio ($\varrho$).
important_parameters: The experiment operates in the detuned Heitler regime ($s \ll 1$) and relies on suppressing the mean field ($\alpha$) to isolate the quantum fluctuations ($\hat{\epsilon}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to effectively suppress the strong mean field ($\alpha$) using optical filtering to probe the weak quantum fluctuation field ($\hat{\epsilon}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the field decomposition into mean and fluctuation components, the experimental setup involving the cavity and three-photon interferometer, and quantitative results showing the violation of the Svetlichny inequality and the QSS protocol implementation.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by decomposing the scattered field, details the experimental setup using cavity QED and filtering, presents measurements of higher-order correlations, confirms entanglement via inequality violation, and concludes with a demonstration of a quantum information application (QSS).
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamentally simple, cavity-enhanced route to generate high-order entangled states directly from a well-understood process (resonance fluorescence), which is highly relevant for quantum optics and quantum information applications.

Resonance fluorescence in the Heitler regime. a, Interference of mean field and quantum fluctuation re- sults in the observation of single-photon emission. b, Inten- sity spectrum of resonance fluorescence under detuned Heitler regime. The mean field spectrum is a delta-like function cen- tered at driving laser frequency ωL, The quantum fluctuation spectrum comprises three Lorentzian peaks: two sidebands at ωL ± ∆with widths Γ, and a weak central carrier at ωL of width 2Γ. The weakness of the carrier’s intensity is due to the absence of this component in two-photon scattering. c, Three-photon inelastic scattering involving three virtual en- ergy levels.

FIG. 2. Experimental setup and observation of three- and four-order photon bunching. a, A single 87Rb atom is trapped at the center of the optical cavity by a two-dimensional optical lattice formed by 850 nm and 796 nm laser beams. The atom is continuously driven by two red-detuned laser beams counter-propagating at an angle. The scattered light from the atom is efficiently collected by the fiber-coupled cavity and guided through the fiber to the measurement setup. b, The scattered light is first sent to a narrow-linewidth notch filter cavity to isolate the quantum fluctuation field, and then directed into a three-photon Franson interferometer for entanglement analysis.
